summary.text: This opportunity briefing examines a framework combining VQ-VAE, motion generation, and prediction for motion forecasting and trajectory prediction in autonomous systems. By leveraging a VQ-VAE to learn shape-aware motion primitives as discrete intention queries, the approach helps address limitations where existing predictors overlook lane topology adherence. A feasibility-aware intention selector further guides the decoder to prioritize topology-consistent intentions while preserving behavioral diversity.

target_user.text: Academic researchers and developers working on autonomous driving systems and motion forecasting models.

jtbd.text: Perform motion forecasting and trajectory prediction that adheres to lane topology and physical or logical constraints for autonomous systems.

value_prop.text: Anchors multimodal predictions to structured motion primitives to improve prediction feasibility and reliability for safety-critical planning.

riskiest_assumption.text: The viability axis score is 1.0, indicating that customers are unwilling or unable to pay for a VQ-VAE-based topology-aware motion prediction framework.

mvp.text: Conduct customer interviews and price acceptance tests with autonomous vehicle software teams to evaluate willingness to pay for topology-aware motion prediction tools, targeting a proposed acceptance rate of 40 percent at a proposed threshold price of $5,000 per month.
